statement:
Let $t_{k-1}(n)$ denote the maximum number of edges in a $K_{k-1}$-free graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\tau_k(G)$ be the minimum size of a vertex set meeting every copy of $K_k$ in $G$. For a balanced partition $V_1\cup\cdots\cup V_{k-1}$ of $[n]$, assume $|V_1|\geq\cdots\geq|V_{k-1}|$. **Xiao and Katona's conjecture.** For fixed integers $k\geq4$ (and as stated in the source, $s>t\geq1$), every graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $t_{k-1}(n)+1$ edges and $\tau_k(G)\geq2$ contains at least

$$
\left(|V_1|+|V_2|-2\right)\prod_{i=3}^{k-1}|V_i|
$$

copies of $K_k$. The paper states that it gives a counterexample to one Xiao–Katona conjecture and proves a modified version, so this original conjecture is refuted.
title: Xiao and Katona's clique-covering conjecture
technical_disposition: The literal definition uses K_(k-1)-free for t_(k-1), whereas the usual threshold for K_k is the (k-1)-partite Turan graph. The unused s>t parameters and contrary resolution text need original passage reconciliation. No wording correction merits credit; no primary body read.

statement:
Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ positive semi-definite Hermitian matrix, and let $1\leq k<n$. For $k$-element subsets $I,J\subset[n]$, define $\mathscr{C}_k(A)$ by

$$
(\mathscr{C}_k(A))_{I,J}=\operatorname{per}(A[I,J])\operatorname{per}(A[I^c,J^c]).
$$

**Pate's conjecture.** The largest eigenvalue of $\mathscr{C}_k(A)$ is $\operatorname{per}(A)$. This conjecture is refuted; the paper states that its $k=1$ case has an $8\times8$ counterexample and presents a new $5\times5$ rank-$2$ counterexample.
title: Pate's conjecture on the largest eigenvalue of the complementary-permanent matrix
technical_disposition: Primary v5 Conjecture 2 and Section 4 supply a PSD Gram matrix H=vv*+uu*, per(H)=504, and a C_2(H) Rayleigh quotient 512. This negates the universal n,k assertion, not just a POT proxy. Selected construction and tensor calculation read; earlier lemmas not fully audited. Public refutation defeats eligibility.

statement:
Let $J_n(x)$ be the finite linear Jaco graph of order $n$, and let $\Delta(J_n(x))$ denote its maximum degree. A sequence is **$p$-graphical** for a graph family $\mathcal{F}$ when it gives the values of a graph parameter $p$ on the members of $\mathcal{F}$. **Maximum-degree formula conjecture.** For $n=2,3,4,\dots$, the maximum degrees are given by sequence A319433, with

$$
\Delta(J_n(x))=\left\lfloor\frac{2(n+2)}{1+\sqrt{5}}\right\rfloor-1.
$$

Moreover, sequence A319433 is $p$-graphical for $p(G)=\Delta(G)$ and $\mathcal{F}=\{G:G=J_n(x),\ n=1,2,3,\dots\}$. The conjecture reduces to proving the stated floor-function identity relating the maximum degree to the vertex-degree formula; its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
title: Maximum-degree formula conjecture for finite linear Jaco graphs
technical_disposition: The literal full record contains an actual public proof dated 2026-08-20, not merely a status label: indegree floor((i+1)/phi^2), degree min(i,n-floor((i+1)/phi)), and threshold Delta>=r iff (r+1)phi<n+2. This is a full-scope public proof route using an established indegree formula; redoing its elementary floor argument is not discovery. Primary Jaco manuscript and indegree dependency not read here.

statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, possibly with multiple edges but no loops, and let $\Delta(G)$ and $\delta(G)$ denote its maximum and minimum degrees. A matching is **maximum** if it has largest possible cardinality, and a vertex is **$M$-unsaturated** if it is not incident with an edge of $M$.

**Mkrtchyan–Petrosyan–Vardanyan conjecture.** If

$$
\Delta(G)-\delta(G)\le 1,
$$

then $G$ contains a maximum matching $M$ such that no two $M$-unsaturated vertices have a common neighbor.

The conjecture is refuted: Picouleau found a counterexample that is a simple bipartite graph with $\delta(G)=4$ and $\Delta(G)=5$.
title: Mkrtchyan–Petrosyan–Vardanyan conjecture on maximum matchings
technical_disposition: Near-regularity allows arbitrary multigraphs, so a simple bipartite degree-4/5 example suffices to refute. Literal record attributes just such a public Picouleau witness. No original witness body checked here; HOLD public-refutation lead rather than claiming fresh certificate or validated exclusion.

statement: For every integer $n \ge 0$, every real number $K \ge 1$, and every nonempty set $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ satisfying $\lvert A+A\rvert \le K\lvert A\rvert$, there exist a subspace $H \le \mathbb{F}_2^n$ and elements $x_1,\ldots,x_m \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$ such that $\lvert H\rvert \le \lvert A\rvert$, $m \le 2K^{12}$, and $A \subseteq \bigcup_{i=1}^{m}(x_i+H)$.
title: Polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture
technical_disposition: Quantifiers n>=0,K>=1 require polynomial covering of every small-doubling set, not an instance. Supplied source is a formalization repository; prohibited GitHub access and unavailable current registry leave source/prior HOLD. No new covering mechanism.

statement:
Let $P(M)$ be the matroid polytope of $M$. **Conjecture 1.**

- The coefficients of the Ehrhart polynomial of $P(M)$ are positive.
- The $h^*$-vector of $P(M)$ is unimodal.

The conjecture is true for all uniform matroids of rank $\le 2$, all uniform matroids with $|E| \le 75$, and all matroids with $|E| \le 9$.
title: Positivity of Matroids
technical_disposition: Two assertions over all matroids; a negative Ehrhart coefficient alone would refute the conjunction, but small uniform cases are insufficient. Sparse-paving counterexample literature is a prior lead, not body-verified here. No constructed polytope or exact Ehrhart certificate; HOLD.

statement: Consider the directed random graph on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ in which each vertex independently chooses one of its four nearest-neighbour directions uniformly, places an arrow in that direction, and independently places an arrow in the opposite direction with probability $\epsilon\in[0,1]$. Let $C^+_\epsilon(0)$ be the forward cluster of the origin, consisting of vertices reachable from $0$ by following arrows, and define $\epsilon_c:=\inf\{\epsilon\in[0,1]:\mathbb{P}(|C^+_\epsilon(0)|=\infty)>0\}$. Determine the exact value of $\epsilon_c$.
title: Critical-parameter question for planar soft-stick percolation
technical_disposition: Exact epsilon_c for independent oriented sticks requires a sharp infinite-cluster threshold, not a Peierls one-sided bound or a finite lattice simulation. Coupling supplies monotonicity but not its value. No tractable full-scope route; primary body unread.

statement: Determine whether the uniform Turán density of the tetrahedron satisfies $\pi_u\!\left(K_4^{(3)}\right)=\frac{1}{2}$. Here $K_4^{(3)}$ is the complete $3$-uniform hypergraph on $4$ vertices, and $\pi_u(H)$ is the supremum of the real numbers $d$ such that, for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large $n$, there exists an $H$-free $3$-uniform hypergraph $G$ on $n$ vertices for which every subset $U\subseteq V(G)$ with $|U|\geq\varepsilon n$ satisfies $e(G[U])\geq(d-\varepsilon)\binom{|U|}{3}$.
title: Erdős–Sós question on the uniform Turán density of K4^(3)
technical_disposition: The epsilon/all-sufficiently-large-n definition requires a uniform extremal upper bound as well as a construction. A finite tetrahedron-free example cannot certify pi_u=1/2. Source claims a result but no body inspected; HOLD public-result lead.

statement: For every integer $n\geq 1$, let $r_n\in(0,1)$ be the unique solution of $r_n^n\bigl(1+n(1+r_n)\bigr)=1$, and set $\bar h_n=1+r_n$. For every $L$-smooth convex function $f$ and gradient-descent iterates $x_{k+1}=x_k-(\bar h_n/L)\nabla f(x_k)$, determine whether the constant schedule $(\bar h_n,\ldots,\bar h_n)$ is $s$-composable at horizon $n$, equivalently whether it satisfies the sharp mixed terminal Lyapunov inequality conjectured by Grimmer, Shu, and Wang. The supplied source does not state the Lyapunov inequality explicitly.
title: Constant-schedule s-composability conjecture
technical_disposition: The statement omits the defining terminal Lyapunov inequality, so s-composability is not an explicit predicate to test. Algebraic r_n and quadratic objectives cannot replace all L-smooth convex functions at every horizon. Definition/source HOLD.

statement: Let $c\phi_{18}(n)$ denote the number of $18$-colored generalized Frobenius partitions of $n$. Prove that, for every integer $n\geq 0$, $c\phi_{18}(30n+19)\equiv 0\pmod{16}$ and $c\phi_{18}(30n+25)\equiv 0\pmod{16}$.
title: Das–Nath–Sarma congruences for generalized Frobenius partitions
technical_disposition: Both arithmetic progressions and every n>=0 require an exact generating-function congruence or a modular-form finite bound with proved hypotheses. A prefix check is not full scope. No source body or modular identity inspected; HOLD prior/source.

statement: For every nontrivial finite abelian group $G$, let $\mathsf d(G)$ denote the maximum length of a zero-sum-free sequence over $G$. Let $\nu(G)$ be the least integer $\ell$ such that every zero-sum-free sequence $T$ over $G$ with $|T|\geq \ell$ satisfies: the set of all nonzero elements of $G$ that are not sums of nonempty subsequences of $T$ is contained in a proper coset of a subgroup of $G$. Gao's conjecture asserts that $\nu(G)=\mathsf d(G)-1$ for every nontrivial finite abelian group $G$.
title: Gao’s conjecture on the invariant ν(G)
technical_disposition: All nontrivial finite abelian groups, all long zero-sum-free sequences, and one proper coset must be handled. Cyclic or small-group enumeration cannot settle arbitrary rank. Boundary d(G)-1 and proper-coset definition need source check; no uniform structural route.

statement: Fix $0<\alpha,r<\infty$. For every $0<p,q\leq\infty$, determine whether, for every $f\in C^1([-1,1])$ satisfying $f(0)=0$ and $|f'(t)|\lesssim |t|^\alpha$, and every real sequence $\lambda\in\ell^r$ with $\|\lambda\|_{\ell^\infty}\leq 1$, the Schur--Hadamard multiplier $S_{\Psi_{f,\lambda}}$ is bounded from $\mathcal{S}^q$ to $\mathcal{S}^p$, where $\Psi_{f,\lambda}=\left(\frac{f(\lambda_i)-f(\lambda_j)}{\lambda_i-\lambda_j}\right)_{i,j}$ with diagonal entries $\Psi_{f,\lambda}(i,i)=f'(\lambda_i)$. Arazy's conjecture asserts that this boundedness holds for every such $f$ and $\lambda$ exactly when $\frac{1}{p}\leq\frac{\alpha}{r}+\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{q}\right\}$.
title: Arazy’s conjecture concerning Schur multipliers
technical_disposition: Needs both sufficiency and necessity for all p,q including quasi-Banach and infinity endpoints, all admissible C1 functions and l^r spectra. Entrywise derivative bounds do not imply the Schatten multiplier estimates. No short full-scope certificate; primary definitions/proofs unread.

statement: Let $(X_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a sequence of random variables and let $(a_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be nonnegative numbers, with $A_n:=\sum_{k=1}^n a_k\to\infty$. Assume that there is a constant $C<\infty$ such that, for every $1\le m\le n$, $\mathbb{E}\left|\sum_{k=m}^n X_k\right|^2\le C\sum_{k=m}^n a_k$. Determine exactly which non-decreasing functions $\psi$ have the universal property that every such admissible sequence satisfies $\sum_{k=1}^n X_k=O\!\left(\sqrt{A_n}\,\psi(A_n)\right)$ almost surely. The characterization is required to hold uniformly over the entire class described by the consecutive-block second-moment hypothesis.
title: Universal normalization problem for the Gál–Koksma lemma
technical_disposition: Universal block-second-moment control allows dependent, non-centered variables. Martingale or independence maximal inequalities cannot be substituted. Necessity needs sharp adverse sequences as well as a uniform a.s. upper bound for every admissible clock; no full route.

statement: Let $\mathcal{C}_{\alpha}$ denote the $\alpha$-Cauchy distribution for $1<\alpha\leq 2$. Determine exactly for which values of $\alpha$ the law $\mathcal{C}_{\alpha}$ is self-decomposable; that is, for every $c\in(0,1)$, whether there exists a probability law $\nu_c$ such that $\mathcal{C}_{\alpha}=D_c\mathcal{C}_{\alpha}*\nu_c$, where $D_c$ denotes scaling by $c$. The claimed classification is $\mathcal{C}_{\alpha}$ is self-decomposable if and only if $\alpha=2$. The associated application asks whether, for a symmetric stable process of index $1<\alpha<2$ started at $0$ and a nonzero point $x$, the first hitting time $T_x=\inf\{t\geq 0:X_t=x\}$ is self-decomposable; the cited preprint claims that it is not.
title: Self-decomposability of α-Cauchy distributions
technical_disposition: The alpha-Cauchy law is not defined in the literal text; full classification alpha in (1,2] plus stable hitting times needs Levy/self-decomposability criteria. Characteristic-function numerical checks or the endpoint alpha=2 do not suffice. Definition/source HOLD.

statement: For every pair of integers $f\ge 1$ and $g>f$, define the increasing sequence $S_{f,g}=(a_n)_{n\ge 1}$ by $a_1=f$, $a_2=g$, and, recursively, $a_{n+1}$ is the smallest integer greater than $a_n$ that is not the sum of two distinct earlier terms; that is, $a_{n+1}=\min\{m>a_n:m\ne a_i+a_j\text{ for all }1\le i<j\le n\}$. Then the sequence of first differences $d_n=a_{n+1}-a_n$ is ultimately periodic: there exist integers $N\ge 1$ and $p\ge 1$ such that $d_{n+p}=d_n$ for every $n\ge N$.
title: Ultimate periodicity of 2-sumfree sequences
technical_disposition: All initial pairs f<g require a proved eventual finite-state reduction with a bound, not periodic-looking prefixes. Exclusion by all distinct earlier sums retains unbounded memory. No state closure mechanism established; primary and successor bodies unread.

statement:
For every finite set $X$ and every hereditary family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq 2^X$—that is, $A\in\mathcal{F}$ and $B\subseteq A$ imply $B\in\mathcal{F}$—every intersecting subfamily $\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathcal{F}$ satisfies
$$
|\mathcal{A}|\leq \max_{x\in X}\bigl|\{A\in\mathcal{F}:x\in A\}\bigr|,
$$
where intersecting means that $A\cap B\neq\varnothing$ for all $A,B\in\mathcal{A}$. Equivalently, $\mathcal{F}$ has a largest intersecting subfamily that is a star.
title: Chvátal’s conjecture
technical_disposition: Hereditary families need a global star extremizer; compression for uniform or shifted families alone does not extend automatically to all downsets. Tiny downset enumeration cannot prove all finite X. No injection establishing the star bound; prior/source HOLD.

statement: For $n\ge 2$, fix an incident direction $\theta_0\in\mathbb S^{n-1}$. Determine whether a compactly supported potential $q$ is uniquely determined by its far-field pattern $u_q^\infty(\omega,\theta_0,k)$ for all observation directions $\omega\in\mathbb S^{n-1}$ and all wavenumbers $k>0$; equivalently, whether $u_{q_1}^\infty(\omega,\theta_0,k)=u_{q_2}^\infty(\omega,\theta_0,k)$ for every $\omega\in\mathbb S^{n-1}$ and $k>0$ implies $q_1=q_2$.
title: Fixed-angle scattering uniqueness problem of Rakesh and Salo
technical_disposition: One fixed incident direction, every frequency and observation direction, arbitrary compact potentials: Born linearization or small-potential uniqueness does not settle nonlinear full scope. No controlled full inverse-scattering mechanism; body unread.

statement: Let $\Pi$ be the set of all bivariate copulas. For $C\in\Pi$, define Spearman's rho and Gini's gamma by $\rho(C)=12\int_0^1\int_0^1 C(u,v)\,du\,dv-3$ and $\gamma(C)=4\int_0^1\bigl(C(u,u)+C(u,1-u)-u\bigr)\,du$. Determine exactly the attainable region $\mathcal R=\{(\rho(C),\gamma(C)):C\in\Pi\}\subseteq[-1,1]^2$, including an explicit description of its boundary and copulas attaining every boundary point.
title: Spearman–Gini exact-region problem
technical_disposition: Exact attainable rho/gamma region needs global inequalities and boundary-attaining copulas for every boundary point. Convex combinations give feasible points, not sharp boundary. Could use optimal transport but no finite extremal reduction proved; body unread.

statement: Let $\chi_{\mathrm{lat}}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ denote the minimum number of colors in a lattice coloring of $\mathbb{R}^n$ such that no two points of the same color are at Euclidean distance $1$. The conjecture asserts that $\chi_{\mathrm{lat}}(\mathbb{R}^4)=49$ and $\chi_{\mathrm{lat}}(\mathbb{R}^5)=140$; equivalently, there are lattice colorings with $49$ and $140$ colors, respectively, and no lattice colorings with fewer colors.
title: Arman–Bondarenko–Prymak–Radchenko lattice-coloring optimality conjecture
technical_disposition: Existence of 49/140-color lattice constructions does not prove their optimality over all lattice colorings in dimensions 4 and 5. Definition of lattice coloring and a full lattice lower-bound classification are missing here. No small certificate full route.

statement: Let $\mathbb N=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$. For an integer $k>1$, a set $A\subseteq\mathbb N$, and $n\in\mathbb N$, define $R_{1,k}(A,n)=\#\{(a_1,a_2)\in A^2:a_1+ka_2=n\}$. For integers $k>1$ and $t\ge 1$, let $f_k(t)$ be the number of sets $A\subseteq\mathbb N$ such that $R_{1,k}(A,n)=R_{1,k}(\mathbb N\setminus A,n)$ for every integer $n\ge t$. Determine whether, for every pair of integers $k,l>1$, there exists an integer $t_0$ such that $f_k(t)=f_l(t)$ for all integers $t\ge t_0$.
title: Yang–Chen problem on weighted representation functions
technical_disposition: Primary v1 Problem 1.1, Theorem 1.2, Corollaries 1.3-1.4, and Section 3 provide f_k(t) asymptotic order 2^t/t^(k/2). For k<l the ratio tends to infinity, directly contradicting eventual equality. Boundary sign-vector counting proof read, Lemmas 2.1-2.6 not fully audited. Existing full-scope public negative result.

statement: For every integer $n>14$, there exist an odd prime $p$ and positive integers $x,y$ such that $n=p+x^2+y^2$.
title: Prime plus two positive squares conjecture
technical_disposition: Universal n>14 requires all integers, not a finite search with positive squares and odd prime. Analytic exceptions and a certified finite cutoff would be substantial, and source claims a result. No primary body read or all-n mechanism; HOLD.

statement:
For the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations $\partial_t u+(u\cdot
abla)u=-
abla p+
u\Delta u$, $
abla\cdot u=0$, with $
u>0$ and smooth divergence-free initial data $u(0,x)=u_0(x)$, determine whether every smooth solution remains smooth for all $t\ge 0$, or whether there exist smooth initial data for which a finite-time singularity occurs. For the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations $\partial_t u+(u\cdot
abla)u=-
abla p$, $
abla\cdot u=0$, determine whether there exist smooth divergence-free initial data and a finite time $T<\infty$ such that the solution becomes singular as $t\uparrow T$; equivalently, whether every smooth Euler solution remains smooth for all $t\ge 0$.
title: Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness and Euler blow-up problems
technical_disposition: Contains two independent global PDE regularity questions; no domain/decay conditions are specified. A forcing or weak-solution example cannot replace smooth finite-time blowup for the intended equations. No tractable complete mechanism; source/definitions HOLD.

statement: Let $\mathcal{O}_{n,m}$ be the set of partitions $\lambda$ of $n$ whose parts are odd and whose largest part satisfies $\lambda_1\le m$, and let $\mathcal{D}_{n,m}$ be the set of partitions of $n$ into distinct parts with $\lambda_1\le m$. If $h_2(\lambda)$ denotes the number of cells of the Ferrers diagram of $\lambda$ having hook length $2$, then the hook-pair conjecture asserts that, for all $n,m\ge 0$, $\displaystyle \sum_{\lambda\in\mathcal{O}_{n,m}}\binom{h_2(\lambda)}{2}\ge \sum_{\lambda\in\mathcal{D}_{n,m}}\binom{h_2(\lambda)}{2}$. Berkovich and Dhar also formulated a stronger coefficientwise inequality for the corresponding hook-length generating functions; the supplied source does not state that inequality explicitly.
title: Berkovich–Dhar hook-length conjectures
technical_disposition: Primary v1 Theorem 1.5 gives odd largest part <=2L-1 versus distinct <=2L; the following common-bound paragraph explicitly specializes to the literal inequality. For m>=1 use L=ceil(m/2), restrict distinct bound to m; m=0 is empty/zero. Selected Glaisher injection and hook-map passage read; full proof/dependencies not audited. Existing stronger result defeats eligibility.

statement:
For every unitarily invariant matrix norm $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{ui}}$, does there exist a constant $c>0$, independent of $n$ and of $G\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$, such that
$$
\min_{P\in\mathcal{P}_n}\|P\circ G\|_{\mathrm{ui}}^2\leq c\,\min_{W\in\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})}\|W\circ G\|_{\mathrm{ui}}\,\|W^{-1}\circ G^{\mathsf{T}}\|_{\mathrm{ui}}?
$$
Here $\mathcal{P}_n$ is the set of $n\times n$ permutation matrices and $\circ$ denotes the Hadamard product. The reverse inequality is known in the opposite direction without a constant: the second minimum is at most the first. In the Frobenius-norm case, equality holds for every $G$, so the optimal constant is $c=1$.
title: Li’s Hadamard-product eigenvalue-perturbation conjecture
technical_disposition: Primary v1 Theorem 2.1(b), Corollary 2.1, Section 4, and Corollary 5.1 give precisely the dimension-uniform Frobenius-equivalence criterion and Frobenius equality. The literal assertion for every unitarily invariant norm is defeated by spectral norms not uniformly Frobenius-equivalent. Repeating that necessity bridge is a routine source adaptation; predecessor Romeo-Tilli body not separately read.

statement: For each integer $n\ge 0$, determine whether there exists a bijection $A:\{0,1\}^n\to\{1,\ldots,2^n\}$ such that, for every pair of distinct coordinates $i,j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and every choice of the remaining coordinates, the face sum $\sum_{(\varepsilon_i,\varepsilon_j)\in\{0,1\}^2}A(x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1},\varepsilon_i,x_{i+1},\ldots,x_{j-1},\varepsilon_j,x_{j+1},\ldots,x_n)$ is independent of the chosen $2$-dimensional face. Classify all such arrangements up to the natural transformations described in the source. The cited paper claims existence for every $n$ and uniqueness up to transformations of size $2^n(n+1)!$ when $n$ is even and $2^n n\,n!$ when $n$ is odd.
title: Coxeter’s question on most-perfect magic squares and magic-faced hypercubes
technical_disposition: Primary v1 Theorem 1 exactly gives all n>=0, existence and parity-dependent symmetry classification/counts. Selected Fourier support proof and even/odd subset-sum reduction read; Lemmas 16-17 complete proof bodies not read. This already states the full target as a theorem, so constructing another hypercube or formalizing it earns no discovery.

statement: For every dimension $d\in\mathbb{N}$ and smoothing parameter $\beta>0$, determine the complete spectral decomposition of the Henze–Wagner covariance-kernel integral operator $\widetilde A_{\beta,d}$ on its Gaussian-weighted Hilbert space: all eigenvalues with their multiplicities, all eigenfunctions, the null space, and all exceptional parameter cases. Equivalently, determine the full spectral data governing the limiting null distribution of the multivariate BHEP normality test.
title: All-dimensional spectral problem for BHEP operators
technical_disposition: Every dimension and beta requires multiplicities, eigenfunctions, null space and exceptional collisions for an operator not explicitly specified here. A Gaussian/Hermite diagonalization of an uncorrected kernel is insufficient for the Henze-Wagner corrections. Definition and body HOLD.

statement: Determine the set of thresholds $\delta>0$ for which there exists a constant $C_M(\delta)<\infty$, independent of the locally compact abelian group $G$, such that every measure $\mu\in M(G)$ satisfying $\|\mu\|_{M(G)}\le 1$ and $\inf_{\gamma\in\widehat G}|\widehat\mu(\gamma)|\ge\delta$ is invertible in $M(G)$ and satisfies $\|\mu^{-1}\|_{M(G)}\le C_M(\delta)$. The claimed sharp answer is that this property holds for every $\delta>\tfrac12$ and fails for $\delta\le\tfrac12$.
title: Nikolski’s norm-controlled inversion problem
technical_disposition: Uniformity is over all locally compact abelian groups and all measures with spectral lower bound, including a sharp failure side at 1/2. Finite-group inversion cannot establish the measure-algebra Wiener-Pitt boundary. Source result lead unread; no full route.

statement: Let $B_1,\ldots,B_n$ be independent Bernoulli random variables with parameters $p_1,\ldots,p_n\in[0,1]$, let $S=\sum_{i=1}^n B_i$, and write $P_k(p)=\mathbb{P}_p(S=k)$. Determine the orders $q>0$ for which, for every $n$, the Rényi entropy $H_q^{\mathrm{R}}(S)=\frac{1}{1-q}\log\!\left(\sum_k P_k(p)^q\right)$ and the Tsallis entropy $H_q^{\mathrm{T}}(S)=\frac{1}{1-q}\left(\sum_k P_k(p)^q-1\right)$ are jointly concave functions of $p=(p_1,\ldots,p_n)$. The claimed sharp answer is that both entropies are jointly concave for every $0<q\leq 1$, while joint concavity fails for every $q>1$, already when $n=2$.
title: Hillion–Johnson critical-order conjectures for the Shepp–Olkin concavity problem
technical_disposition: Both Renyi and Tsallis joint concavity must hold over every Bernoulli parameter cube and every n. The q=1 formulas need limiting definitions, a wording issue without credit. A Hessian at n=2 addresses only failure at one q unless a uniform family is proved. Do not confuse accepted Renyi-increment family with this statement; no source body checked.

statement: Let $A_\Gamma$ be an Artin group and let $W_\Gamma$ be its associated Coxeter group, obtained from $A_\Gamma$ by imposing $s_i^2=1$ for every standard generator $s_i$. For a group $G$ admitting finite non-abelian quotients, let $m(G)=\min\{|Q|:Q\text{ is a finite non-abelian quotient of }G\}$. The conjecture asserts that the isomorphism classes of finite non-abelian quotients $Q$ of $A_\Gamma$ with $|Q|=m(A_\Gamma)$ are exactly the isomorphism classes of finite non-abelian quotients $Q$ of $W_\Gamma$ with $|Q|=m(W_\Gamma)$. Equivalently, a smallest finite non-abelian quotient of $A_\Gamma$ is isomorphic to a smallest finite non-abelian quotient of $W_\Gamma$.
title: Smallest nonabelian quotient conjecture for Artin groups
technical_disposition: General Artin/Coxeter groups may fail to admit the finite nonabelian quotients required by m(G); domain qualification needs source reconciliation. Coxeter factor quotients give only one inequality, not minimal Artin quotient classification. No general minimal-quotient bridge.

statement: For every finite group $G$, there exists a finite lattice $L$ such that $\operatorname{Aut}(L)\cong G$ and the action of $\operatorname{Aut}(L)$ on the elements of $L$ has at most $C$ orbits, where $C$ is an absolute constant independent of $G$. Equivalently, if $\lambda(G)$ denotes the minimum number of $\operatorname{Aut}(L)$-orbits on $L$, taken over all finite lattices $L$ with $\operatorname{Aut}(L)\cong G$, then $\sup_G\lambda(G)<\infty$.$
title: Babai–Goodman bounded-orbit lattice conjecture
technical_disposition: The orbit bound C must be absolute for every finite group; Frucht-style constructions with size depending on G do not control lattice automorphism orbit count. No uniform lattice gadget construction with proved automorphism rigidity and bounded orbits; source unread.

statement:
For the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations $\partial_t u+(u\cdot
abla)u=-
abla p+
u\Delta u+f$, $
abla\cdot u=0$, with smooth divergence-free initial data $u(0,x)=u_0(x)$ of finite energy and smooth forcing $f$, determine whether the solution remains smooth for every finite time, or whether there exist such data and forcing for which a smooth solution develops a singularity at some finite time $T<\infty$.
title: Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness problem
technical_disposition: Smooth finite-energy forced 3D Navier-Stokes all finite times remains full analytic regularity scope. Arbitrary smooth forcing without spatial growth/decay specifications needs primary reconciliation; not an eligibility opportunity from wording. No proof or counterexample mechanism.

statement: For every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a constant $c_{\varepsilon}>0$ such that, for every sufficiently large $n$, every integer $d\leq (1-\varepsilon)n/2$, and every $d$-regular graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, the bisection width satisfies $\operatorname{bw}(G)\leq dn/4-c_{\varepsilon}d^{1/3}n$, where $\operatorname{bw}(G)=\min e_G(S,V(G)\setminus S)$ and the minimum is over all $S\subseteq V(G)$ with $\bigl||S|-|V(G)\setminus S|\bigr|\leq 1$.
title: Räty–Sudakov–Tomon bisection-width conjecture
technical_disposition: Need a positive c_epsilon uniform in n,d and every regular graph below density cutoff, with balanced parts. Random bisection gives dn/4-scale but not the d^(1/3)n improvement. No full discrepancy argument; source claimed theorem body unread.

statement: For every edge-color-critical graph $F$ with $\chi(F)=r+1$, and every positive integer $n$, let $\mathcal{G}_{n,r}(F)$ be the family of all $n$-vertex, $F$-free graphs that are not $r$-partite. The Fang–Lin conjecture asserts that every graph in $\mathcal{G}_{n,r}(F)$ having maximum adjacency spectral radius also has the maximum number of edges; equivalently, $\operatorname{SPEX}_{r}(n,F)\subseteq \operatorname{EX}_{r}(n,F)$. The cited preprint claims that this fails for $F=K_1\vee\mu(K_3)$, for which $\chi(F)=5$: for all sufficiently large $n$, no non-$4$-partite, $F$-free $n$-vertex graph simultaneously maximizes the edge count and the adjacency spectral radius, i.e. $\operatorname{SPEX}_{4}(n,F)\cap\operatorname{EX}_{4}(n,F)=\varnothing$.
title: Fang–Lin conjecture
technical_disposition: A single fixed color-critical F can refute all-F assertion, but must prove the large-n extremizers differ, not exhibit two graphs with opposite order. Source already names K1 join Mycielski(K3) and eventual disjoint extremizer sets. Body-unverified public-refutation lead; no new certificate proposed.

statement: For which integers $r\ge 0$ does there exist a finite simple $r$-regular graph $G$ such that, for every vertex $v\in V(G)$, the triangle-degree $\tau_G(v)=\left|\{\{x,y\}\subseteq V(G):xy\in E(G),\,vx,vy\in E(G)\}\right|$ is distinct from $\tau_G(w)$ for every other vertex $w\in V(G)$? Equivalently, determine whether such a graph exists for each $r$; the claimed classification is that one exists if and only if $r\ge 9$.
title: Existence of regular K3-irregular graphs
technical_disposition: Same triangle-degree regularity classification as assigned 406325 with a different cited preprint. Degree counting gives only preliminary necessary bounds, not r=9 construction and all-r extension. Trivial empty/single-vertex exceptions are domain corrections without credit. No source body checked.

statement:
Prove that the one-dimensional isotropic antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chain has a positive spectral gap for every integer spin S >= 1 and is gapless for every half-integer spin.

Source: [Marius Lemm and Angelo Lucia, On the critical finite-size gap scaling for frustration-free Hamiltonians, Review of Mathematical Physics 37 (2025), introduction.](https://re.public.polimi.it/retrieve/2332a1fb-6d7b-4ef7-a66f-1cbb552b76f8/lemm-lucia-2025-on-the-critical-finite-size-gap-scaling-for-frustration-free-hamiltonians.pdf).

title: The Haldane Conjecture on Spectral Gaps of Antiferromagnetic Quantum Spin Chains
technical_disposition: Integer-spin gap for every S and half-integer gaplessness require thermodynamic spectral statements, not a finite-chain diagonalization or frustration-free surrogate. Primary Hamiltonian and boundary conditions not read; no full analytic route.

statement:
Determine whether every smooth embedding of S^3 in S^4 is smoothly unknotted; equivalently, whether each of its two complementary closures is diffeomorphic to the standard 4-ball B^4.

Source: [Peter Lambert-Cole, "Stein trisections and homotopy 4-balls," arXiv:2104.02003 [math.GT], April 2021.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.02003).

title: Smooth Four-Dimensional Schoenflies Problem
technical_disposition: A smooth embedding of S3 in S4 needs complementary standard smooth 4-balls; topological Schoenflies does not settle the smooth structures. No handle cancellation or complete 4-dimensional classification route; body unread.

statement:
For each complex polynomial T of degree at least two, determine whether T can be approximated by polynomials of the same degree all of whose critical points converge under iteration to attracting periodic cycles, that is, whether hyperbolic polynomials are dense in the space of complex polynomials of each degree.

Source: [Steve Smale, Mathematical Problems for the Next Century, 1998.](https://www.fim.uni-passau.de/fileadmin/dokumente/fakultaeten/fim/lehrstuhl/muller/SmaleProblems1998.pdf).

title: Density of Hyperbolicity for Complex Polynomials
technical_disposition: Density must hold in each fixed complex polynomial degree, including arbitrary recurrent critical dynamics. Real-polynomial or hyperbolic-subclass approximation does not extend automatically. No complete perturbation argument; primary unread.

statement:
Construct an infinite family of quantum locally testable codes with asymptotically constant rate, relative distance, soundness, and local-projector weight, or prove that no such family exists.

Source: [Error Correction Zoo, Quantum locally testable code (QLTC), maintained through 2026, accessed 2026-08-22.](https://errorcorrectionzoo.org/c/qltc).

title: Constant-Parameter Quantum Locally Testable Codes
technical_disposition: All four asymptotic constants must coexist in one infinite quantum code family. A finite code or good qLDPC family without constant soundness is not the target. No robust local-testing construction; source scope/prior HOLD.

statement:
Determine whether every monoid defined by a single defining relation has a solvable word problem: given a one-relation monoid presentation <a_1, ..., a_n | u = v> and two words over the generators, decide whether the two words represent the same element of the monoid; no undecidable one-relation monoid is known and no algorithm solving the general case is known.

Source: [The Word Problem for One-relation Monoids: A Survey (Carl-Fredrik Nyberg-Brodda)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.02853).

title: The Word Problem for One-Relation Monoids
technical_disposition: Requires a terminating decision algorithm for every one-relation monoid and every pair of words. Group Magnus algorithms and special monoid presentations do not imply general monoid decidability. No reduction or finite complete rewriting mechanism; body unread.

statement:
Determine whether the unique solution of every linear complementarity problem with a rational P-matrix and rational right-hand side can be computed in time polynomial in the bit length of the input.

statement:
Determine the maximal number K of mutually unbiased bases in a D-dimensional Hilbert space for non-prime-power composite dimensions D (in particular, decide whether K = 7 MUBs exist in dimension D = 6).

Source: [Daniel McNulty and Stefan Weigert, Mutually Unbiased Bases in Composite Dimensions - A Review, Quantum 10, 2051 (2026), Abstract and Popular summary](https://quantum-journal.org/papers/q-2026-04-01-2051/).

title: Maximal Number of Mutually Unbiased Bases in Composite Dimensions
technical_disposition: All non-prime-power D requires maximal counts; seven bases in D=6 alone is already a difficult exact existence problem. Numerical approximate unbiased bases neither certify existence nor prove nonexistence. No finite algebraic elimination bound established; primary unread.

statement: For every fixed pair of integers $r,k\ge 3$, let $C_k^{(r)}$ denote the $r$-uniform linear cycle with $k$ hyperedges, and let $\operatorname{ex}_r(n,C_k^{(r)})$ be the maximum number of hyperedges in an $n$-vertex $C_k^{(r)}$-free $r$-uniform hypergraph. The conjecture is that, as $n\to\infty$, the number of labelled $n$-vertex $C_k^{(r)}$-free $r$-uniform hypergraphs is $2^{(1+o(1))\operatorname{ex}_r(n,C_k^{(r)})}$; equivalently, $\left|\operatorname{Forb}_r(n,C_k^{(r)})\right|=2^{(1+o(1))\operatorname{ex}_r(n,C_k^{(r)})}$, where $\operatorname{Forb}_r(n,C_k^{(r)})$ is the family of such hypergraphs.
title: Balogh–Narayanan–Skokan counting conjecture for linear-cycle-free hypergraphs
technical_disposition: All fixed r,k>=3 require asymptotically sharp labelled hypergraph counts relative to ex, not just a coarse 2^O(ex) container bound. No balanced supersaturation mechanism that yields the sharp constant; source claimed result body unread.

statement: For the SIRS epidemic model with nonlinear incidence rate $\frac{kI^p}{1+\alpha I^q}$, where $p>0$ and $q\ge 0$ are arbitrary real numbers, determine the largest possible codimension of a generalized Hopf bifurcation at an admissible positive equilibrium, as the remaining model parameters and $p,q$ vary. In particular, decide whether codimension five is maximal, or whether an admissible codimension-six generalized Hopf point exists.
title: Maximum generalized-Hopf codimension in the nonlinear-incidence SIRS model
technical_disposition: An admissible codimension-six point might be a finite algebraic witness, but arbitrary real p,q and unspecified equilibrium/parameter conditions demand actual model and Lyapunov coefficients first. No exact coefficient system or certified admissibility box. Bounded screen stops before expensive elimination.

title: Baricz’s conjecture on Bessel-function Turán inequalities
technical_disposition: All nu>0 and all zero intervals require existence, ordering in n, convergence and strict nu-monotonicity of branch minima. Riccati/Bessel recurrences suggest a route but do not control parameter derivatives of moving minima by themselves. Source result lead unread; no full proof chain.

statement: For every integer $p\ge 2$, determine whether the higher-genus closed Gromov–Witten potentials of the toric Calabi–Yau threefold $X_p=\operatorname{Tot}\!\left(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(p-1)\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(-p-1)\right)$ satisfy the higher-genus ansatz of Caporaso–Griguolo–Mariño–Pasquetti–Seminara and whether their degeneration to the relevant critical regime satisfies the corresponding double-scaling conjecture. The reported verification assumes the nonvanishing condition on the torus weights required for the open–closed mirror-symmetry construction.
title: Caporaso–Griguolo–Mariño–Pasquetti–Seminara higher-genus ansatz and double-scaling conjecture
technical_disposition: Higher-genus ansatz and critical scaling are not explicitly formulated, and nonvanishing torus weights affect scope. Fixed-genus computations or an endpoint correction cannot settle every p and genus. Definitions, primary and dependency HOLD.

statement: Determine all integers $r\ge 0$ for which there exists a finite simple $r$-regular graph $G$ such that the triangle-degrees are pairwise distinct: for every vertex $v\in V(G)$, let $\operatorname{td}_G(v)=\lvert\{\{x,y\}\subseteq V(G):\{v,x,y\}\text{ spans a triangle in }G\}\rvert$; require that $\operatorname{td}_G(u)\ne\operatorname{td}_G(v)$ for all distinct $u,v\in V(G)$. Recent preprints claim that such a graph exists if and only if $r\ge 9$.
title: Regular K3-irregular graph existence problem
technical_disposition: Duplicate mathematical family of assigned 405772, now citing 2610.08478. Full regularity classification r>=9 already reported publicly but body not checked. No new all-r construction; no credit for second record or small examples.

statement: Does there exist a positive integer $N$ such that, for every integer $n\ge N$, the maximum number of edges in a simple solid matching-covered graph on $2n$ vertices is $n^2$? Here a graph is matching-covered if it is connected, has at least two vertices, and every edge belongs to a perfect matching; it is solid if every separating cut is tight, meaning that every perfect matching contains exactly one edge of the cut.
title: Lucchesi–Murty conjecture on simple solid matching-covered graphs
technical_disposition: Eventual maximum n^2 needs both lower construction (complete bipartite) and a sharp upper bound for all simple solid matching-covered graphs. Solids require a separating-cut structural theorem; small brute force cannot establish eventuality. Source claimed result body unread.

statement: For every integer $k\ge 2$ and every finite family $\mathcal{F}$ of finite simple graphs, each having at least one edge, there exists a constant $C=C(k,\mathcal{F})$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$, $\operatorname{sat}_k(n,\operatorname{Berge}\text{-}\mathcal{F})\le Cn$. Here $\operatorname{sat}_k(n,\operatorname{Berge}\text{-}\mathcal{F})$ is the minimum number of hyperedges in a $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices that contains no Berge copy of any graph in $\mathcal{F}$, but such that adding any missing $k$-vertex hyperedge creates a Berge copy of some graph in $\mathcal{F}$; a Berge copy is an injective assignment of the edges of the graph to hyperedges containing their corresponding vertex pairs.
title: English–Gordon–Graber–Methuku–Sullivan Berge saturation conjecture
technical_disposition: All k and all finite forbidden families need a single linear saturation construction preserving Berge-freeness and maximality. Star/core constructions work for special F but are not automatically universal. Source claims linear bound; no body check or new family-independent gadget.

statement: Given a sufficiently regular, possibly nonconstant coefficient matrix field $A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$, consider the fractional-gradient bilinear form $\mathcal{E}_A(u,v)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} A(x)D^s u(x)\cdot D^s v(x)\,dx$. Determine whether there exists a symmetric integral kernel $K_A(x,y)$ such that, for suitable test functions $u,v$, $\mathcal{E}_A(u,v)=\iint_{\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n}(u(x)-u(y))(v(x)-v(y))K_A(x,y)\,dx\,dy$, and in particular whether the representing kernel can be chosen nonnegative, or uniformly positive, under the corresponding positivity assumptions on $A$. The constant-coefficient case has a negative answer to the positivity question, while the general nonconstant-coefficient case remains open.
title: SS18 Open Problem 1.10 on fractional-gradient kernels
technical_disposition: The literal field A is not stated symmetric: antisymmetric A can make E_A nonsymmetric while any symmetric-kernel bilinear form is symmetric. That is a domain correction, not credit. Intended symmetric variable-coefficient kernel/positivity requires nonlocal distribution analysis; constant case already negative publicly. No full intended-scope route.

statement: Let $S_g$ be the closed orientable surface of genus $g$, and let $\delta^{+}_{\mathrm{rev}}(S_g)$ denote the minimum stretch factor among orientation-reversing pseudo-Anosov mapping classes of $S_g$. For every integer $k\geq 2$, $\delta^{+}_{\mathrm{rev}}(S_{2k-1})$ is the largest real root of $x^{4k}-x^{2k+1}-x^{2k-1}-1$, and the even-genus minima satisfy $\delta^{+}_{\mathrm{rev}}(S_{2k})>\delta^{+}_{\mathrm{rev}}(S_{2k-1})$.
title: Orientation-reversing minimal stretch factor conjecture
technical_disposition: Every genus parameter k>=2 needs optimality among all orientation-reversing pseudo-Anosov maps, plus even/odd comparison. Constructing a map with the displayed polynomial gives only an upper bound. Small-genus enumeration is not full scope; primary not read.
